patterns.title: Use CAP-native message lookup
compatibilityChecks: Verify cds.i18n availability in the installed CAP version
Identify messages vs labels vs a custom bundle and locale/placeholder behavior
contraindications: The file is not a CAP translation bundle
Custom fallback semantics must be preserved
patterns.example: const text = cds.i18n.messages.at('ORDER_CONFLICT', req.locale, { ID: req.data.ID })
patterns.verification: Compare locale, fallback, and placeholder outputs against existing tests. For req.reject use message keys directly instead of pre-translating.

patterns.title: Prefer generic CAP pagination
compatibilityChecks: Confirm the generic READ provider handles this entity
Check custom READ handlers, upstream limits, sorting, count, and paging contracts
contraindications: Custom remote pagination protocol
Custom handler bypasses the generic provider
patterns.example:
@cds.query.limit: { default: 20, max: 100 }
service CatalogService { /* preserve existing projections */ }
patterns.verification: Compare first/next/empty page, $top/$skip, sorting, and $count; do not remove custom paging without behavioral tests.

patterns.title: Review upstream error forwarding
compatibilityChecks: Prove the caught error comes from a remote operation, not local validation
Check existing error library, UI5 field targets, error codes, and module format
Distinguish req.error collection from req.reject immediate throwing; the example rejects immediately
Verify the effective CAP version and runtime before adoption
contraindications: An established project wrapper already preserves the required contract
Client contract requires distinct upstream business errors not yet mapped
Collected errors must remain collected; the rejecting example is not a drop-in replacement

helperAlternative.note: Optional, private, and unpublished; a proposal that uses it stays needs-review. The default example needs no dependency. CommonJS consumers require an approved module-loading strategy.

patterns.verification: Test known business errors, unknown upstream failures, localization, field targets, collection vs immediate rejection, and no leakage over real CAP HTTP.

patterns.title: Review remote-service consumption and READ delegation
compatibilityChecks: Resolve the actual configured cds.requires key and service/model mapping; example names are placeholders, not detected project names
Confirm the target is a remote service rather than a database or local CAP service, and that direct HTTP actually consumes its API
Inspect imported model, domain consumption projection, exposed service projection, and existing READ delegation
Verify projection/query translation, protocol, authentication, destination, paging, count, and expand support in the installed CAP version
Check authorization and tenant context, existing client library, and any custom upstream request/response transformation
contraindications: Connection is to a local service or database
Existing consumption projections and delegation already preserve the intended contract
Direct HTTP is not a modeled CAP remote-service API or requires unsupported protocol behavior
Cross-service joins or expands require additional application logic or a separately reviewed replication strategy
patterns.verification: Context-only signal, not a defect. Confirm service identity from configuration, inspect both projection layers, and test query forwarding, mapped fields, filters, paging/count, authorization, and upstream failure with a local mock. A remote association alone does not mandate replication. Never copy credentials or require Cloud SDK packages without checking this CAP version's HTTP client requirements.

patterns.title: Review manual field checks for declarative validation
compatibilityChecks: Prove the condition rejects invalid field input rather than applying a default or branching business logic
Identify the actual service entity, field type, CREATE/UPDATE/action handler, and effective annotations
Compare missing/null/empty/whitespace input, false, zero, and omitted PATCH fields; truthiness is not equivalent to @mandatory
Preserve client-visible error codes, localization, Fiori field targets, and error aggregation
Use @mandatory only for unconditional required input; consider @assert.range or @assert.format only after verifying their support and exact semantics
contraindications: The requirement is conditional, cross-field, authorization-related, or depends on external state
The check supplies a default instead of rejecting input
The existing custom validation library preserves required UI or business semantics not supplied by native annotations
The handler does not use the generic application-service validation pipeline
patterns.verification: Only propose this illustrative annotation after resolving the actual service/field and proving equivalence. Compare valid, missing, null, empty, whitespace, false, zero, partial PATCH, draft, and deep-write cases as applicable; inspect error code, locale, field target, and aggregation. Do not remove custom logic just because a field guard matched.

patterns.title: Review common key and audit-field aspects
compatibilityChecks: Inspect the effective entity and inherited aspects before proposing cuid or managed
A UUID key is already auto-filled by generic CAP providers; cuid is equivalent shorthand, not a required fix
Compare every audit-field name, type, annotation, insertion/update behavior, caller, and database migration
Inspect existing data, foreign keys, projections, generated SQL, and public API before changing the model
contraindications: External or legacy schema owns the keys or audit fields
Custom audit semantics, composite/business keys, or caller-provided values must be retained
An inherited aspect already supplies the intended behavior
Replacing fields would change persistence or API without an approved migration
patterns.verification: Context-only signal. Do not rename keys or add all four managed fields merely to reduce boilerplate. Compare compiled CSN/SQL and service metadata, seed data, CREATE/UPDATE behavior, and migration impact; preserve custom semantics.

patterns.title: Review interpolated query strings for safe parameterization
compatibilityChecks: Prove interpolated content is used as query text and trace whether it can contain untrusted data
Separate data values from identifiers and query structure; parameterization does not authorize dynamic identifiers
Preserve database-specific semantics, null handling, search wildcards, types, authorization filters, and paging
contraindications: The matched method is not a CAP query API
The expression already binds values safely or builds a trusted static fragment
Dynamic identifiers require a validated allowlist or model-based construction rather than value placeholders
patterns.example:
const { Books } = this.entities
const books = await SELECT.from(Books).where({ ID: req.data.ID })
patterns.verification: Candidate, not a confirmed injection finding. Test quotes and SQL-like input as literal data, nulls, numeric values, and existing authorization predicates. Tagged templates are safe when invoked as tags, not when passed as an interpolated string inside parentheses.

patterns.title: Review manual transactions and request-context boundaries
compatibilityChecks: Determine whether this is a managed service handler, standalone script, or background job
Inspect commit/rollback on every error path, awaited work, request context, tenant, and user propagation
Check intended atomicity and isolation before removing or introducing a root transaction
Remote HTTP side effects are not rolled back atomically with a local database transaction
contraindications: An intentional standalone/background transaction already finalizes safely
The application intentionally requires a separate transaction boundary
A matched tx variable is not a CAP transaction
patterns.verification: The example is for an approved standalone boundary; managed service handlers normally already have a transaction. Test commit, rollback, rejected async work, tenant/user isolation, and connection release. Do not claim distributed atomicity or solve reliable remote delivery with a transaction wrapper.

patterns.title: Retain CAP-native draft handling
compatibilityChecks: Inspect service projection, composition tree, existing draft handlers, and UI behavior
contraindications: The annotation alone is not evidence of duplicated boilerplate
patterns.example:
@odata.draft.enabled
entity Orders as projection on db.Orders;
patterns.verification: Context-only candidate: keep the existing implementation unless handler evidence proves redundancy. Never add an internal draft helper based on this signal alone.
